conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and would like to know if I'm eligible.

I have three children. There's Alex, who's 5 years old, Blake who's 17, and Charlie who's 19.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about Alex, Blake, and Charlie.

To help determine your eligibility, I have a few more questions. Let me start with:

Are you responsible for all three children, meaning they live with you and you pay for things like their food, clothes, and other needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, all three of them live with me at home, and I take care of all their needs - food, clothes, everything they need really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that.

Now, since Blake is 17 and Charlie is 19, I need to ask about their current situations:

**For Blake (age 17):** Is Blake currently in full-time education or on an approved training course? If so, could you tell me what type of education or training they're doing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in education at the moment. They finished school but aren't doing any courses or training right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Blake.

**For Charlie (age 19):** Is Charlie currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar) or on an approved training course? And when did they turn 19?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Charlie is in full-time education - they're doing A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Charlie.

Just to clarify a couple more things about Charlie:

1. Did Charlie start their A-levels before they turned 19?
2. When did Charlie turn 19 (approximately which month/year)?

This will help me determine whether Child Benefit can continue for Charlie.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Charlie turned 19 earlier this year, but yes, they started their A-levels well before that - they've been doing them for a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that about Charlie.

One more important question: Are you and all three children living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we all live in the UK - we're in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for each of your three children.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, here is your Child Benefit eligibility for each child:

---

### ✅ **Alex (age 5) — Eligible**
Alex is under 16, lives with you in the UK, and you are responsible for their care. You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

---

### ❌ **Blake (age 17) — Not Eligible**
Although Blake is under 20, they are not currently in full-time education or on an approved training course. For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can only be claimed if they remain in qualifying full-time education or approved training. Since Blake has left school and isn't in any such programme, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Blake at this time.

*Note: If Blake were to return to full-time non-advanced education or start an approved training course, you may become eligible to claim again.*

---

### ✅ **Charlie (age 19) — Eligible**
Even though Charlie is 19, they are in full-time non-advanced education (A-levels) which they started before turning 19. Child Benefit can continue until they finish this course (or turn 20, whichever comes first). You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Charlie.

---

If you have any further questions about the claims process or anything else, please feel free to ask!

Blake is 17 years old but is not currently in full-time education or on an approved training course. Child Benefit can only be claimed for children aged 16-19 if they remain in approved full-time education or training. Since Blake has left school and is not in any qualifying education or training, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Blake.

Charlie is 19 years old but is currently in full-time non-advanced education (A-levels), which they started before turning 19. Child Benefit can continue for young people until they complete their current course of non-advanced education, up until they turn 20, provided they started the course before turning 19. Since Charlie meets these criteria and lives with you in the UK, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Charlie.
